title: Cover the steam-table pans: notched lid over each utensil, solid lid on the others
instruction: Cover the four pans on the steam table. A pan with a serving utensil in it gets a notched lid, turned so the utensil's handle comes out through the notch and the lid sits flat; a pan without a utensil gets a solid lid. Leave the utensils where they are.
context: Cooks and food preparation workers keep hot food in steam tables at 57 C (135 F) or above (US FDA Food Code 3-501.16) and cover the pans between servings to hold the heat and keep debris out. A serving utensil in use may stay in the food with its handle above the food and the container (Food Code 3-304.12(A)), so steam-table pan covers are sold notched: the handle comes out through the notch at the server's side and the cover sits flat. A pan with no utensil gets a solid cover, since a notched one leaves an open slot. The two everyday mistakes are visible and measurable: a solid cover propped open on a ladle's handle, and a notched cover turned the wrong way so its plain end rests on the handle. Here a 1:5 steam-table section holds four pans, two with a utensil; the covers start crosswise beside it, so each needs a quarter turn, and which way it turns decides where a notch ends up.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases (the server's side is toward the arms), y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:5 steam-table section, all fixed: (1) Four full-size (GN 1/1) stainless steel pans, open boxes 106 mm along x by 65 mm along y and 30 mm tall with 3 mm walls, centred at x 33.0 cm: pan 1 at y +12.75 cm, pan 2 at y +4.25, pan 3 at y -4.25, pan 4 at y -12.75 cm (20 mm apart). Each is filled to 8 mm below its rim (22 mm up) with a rigid food stand-in (painted filler): pan 1 dark red-brown chilli, pan 2 white rice, pan 3 yellow sweetcorn, pan 4 green beans. (2) Deck: grey stainless strips 30 mm tall, flush with the rims, round and between the pans: one in front (x 25.7 to 27.7 cm) and one behind (x 38.3 to 40.3 cm), both from y -18 to +18 cm, and five 20 mm strips between them, beside and between the pans (y +16 to +18, +7.5 to +9.5, -1 to +1, -9.5 to -7.5 and -18 to -16 cm). (3) Two serving utensils, clipped so they cannot move: a ladle with a black nylon handle in pan 1 and a slotted spoon with a red nylon handle in pan 3, each on its pan's centre line in three rigid parts: a stainless bowl 24 x 24 x 4 mm lying on the food (x 29.0 to 31.4 cm); a stem 6 mm (x) by 10 mm (y) standing on the food 4 mm behind the front wall (x 28.4 to 29.0 cm), up to 56 mm above the table (26 mm above the rim); and a handle 10 mm wide and 8 mm thick running from the stem's top out over the front rim and deck toward the arms, to x 23.2 cm (56 to 64 mm up). Stem and handle are nylon in the handle's colour. Loose: (4) Four lids (pan covers), rigid 1:5 models in light grey PVC: each a flat plate the pan's size, 106 x 65 x 3 mm, with a black PVC handle bar 50 x 20 x 14 mm fixed on top at its middle, along the plate's length. Two are notched, with a notch 26 mm wide and 25 mm deep cut into the middle of one short end (46 g); two are solid (48 g). They lie flat and crosswise (long side along y) on the table beside the deck: on the left, the notched lid centred at x 37.0, y +27.0 cm with its notch toward +y, and a solid lid at x 25.0, y +27.0 cm; on the right, a solid lid at x 37.0, y -27.0 cm and the notched lid at x 25.0, y -27.0 cm with its notch toward -y. On a centred lid with its notch at the front the stem rises through the notch with 8 mm to spare either side and 12 mm to the notch's end, and the handle runs out above it; a solid lid, or a notched lid turned round, lands on the handle and stands propped open about 20 degrees. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from the lids' poses at the last step, as a top photo and a ruler at each corner of each lid would read it. A lid is seated on a pan when its plate lies flat (tilted 3 degrees or less), every corner of the plate's underside is within 2 mm of the rim top (30 mm up; a lid on top of another lid is at least 3 mm higher and is not seated), the middle of its plate is within 8 mm of the pan's centre seen from above, its long side is within 6 degrees of the pan's, and it is still (no corner moved more than 2 mm over the last 0.5 s); a lid still in a gripper counts as it lies. The right lid for pan 1 or pan 3 (with a utensil) is a notched lid with its notch at the front, toward the arms where the handle comes out (within 6 degrees); for pan 2 or pan 4 (no utensil) it is a solid lid, either way round. Either notched lid may go on either utensil pan and either solid lid on either plain pan. Zero first: the trial scores 0 if any part of either utensil ends more than 5 mm from where it was set (moved, lifted or bent; in the simulation they are fixed). Otherwise each pan with the right lid seated on it earns 0.25, and a pan earns nothing if it is left uncovered, if its lid is not seated (a solid lid or a backwards notched lid propped on the handle, about 20 degrees with its front about 35 mm up; a lid pushed back far enough to clear the handle, 13 mm or more, is more than 8 mm off centre), or if it has no utensil and a notched lid (an open slot). The score is the sum over the four pans: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0, and the trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. Examples: the start 0; all four right 1.0; one utensil pan left uncovered 0.75; one side's two lids swapped (the solid lid propped on the ladle, the notched lid on the rice) 0.5; only one pan right 0.25; any utensil moved 0. In a real trial: a top photo for which lid is on which pan and which way its notch faces, a ruler from the deck at each lid corner, and a mark at each utensil's handle.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The pans, food, deck and utensils are fixed; each utensil is a stepped stand-in of three boxes, and the lids' handle bars are sized for the gripper. Each lid is one rigid body of boxes, so its notch is real and a wrong lid is propped by the handle. Heat and steam are not simulated. The scorer sees only the lids and utensils, not the grippers, so a lid held still on its pan counts as seated.
reset_notes: Lay the four lids flat and crosswise (long side along y) beside the deck: the notched lid centred at x 37.0, y +27.0 cm with its notch toward +y and a solid lid at x 25.0, y +27.0 cm; a solid lid at x 37.0, y -27.0 cm and the notched lid at x 25.0, y -27.0 cm with its notch toward -y. Check each utensil is still clipped where it was set. The pans, food and deck are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
